q: A nutrient cycle is a repeated pathway of a particular nutrient from the physical environment to living organisms and back to the ______.
e: A nutrient cycle is a repeated pathway of a particular nutrient from the physical environment to living organisms and back to the environment. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock. Atmosphere is different: the atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth.

q: The six main nutrient cycles include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorous, and ______.
e: The six main nutrient cycles include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorous, and sulphur. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. Potassium is not sulphur.

q: Nitrogen gas constitutes ______ of the atmosphere.
e: Nitrogen gas constitutes 78% of the atmosphere. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. 21% is not 78%.

q: The enzyme that catalyses the conversion of nitrogen gas into ammonia is called ______.
e: The enzyme that catalyses the conversion of nitrogen gas into ammonia is called nitrogenase. Nitrogenase is the enzyme that fixes nitrogen gas into a usable form. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. Ammoniase is not nitrogenase.

q: Rhizobium forms a mutualistic association with the roots of ______.
e: Rhizobium forms a mutualistic association with the roots of legumes. Legumes host nitrogen-fixing Rhizobium in root nodules. Roots may use air spaces or aerenchyma when soil oxygen is low. Ferns is not legumes.

q: Ammonification is the process by which decomposers break down organic nitrogen to produce ______.
e: Ammonification is the process by which decomposers break down organic nitrogen to produce ammonia. Ammonification is microbes releasing ammonia from dead organic nitrogen. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead material and recycle nutrients.

q: Nitrifying bacteria such as Nitrosomonas convert ammonium ions into ______.
e: Nitrifying bacteria such as Nitrosomonas convert ammonium ions into nitrites. Nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate. Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia to nitrite in nitrification. Nitrates is not nitrites.

Denitrification converts nitrates into nitrogen gas. Nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule. Nitrites is different: nitrites are the middle step as ammonia is oxidised toward nitrate.

q: Phosphorus is a component of biological molecules such as RNA, DNA, phospholipids, and ______.
e: Phosphorus is a component of biological molecules such as RNA, DNA, phospholipids, and ATP. ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. Cellulose is different: cellulose is the beta-glucose polymer that makes plant cell walls rigid.

q: In the phosphorus cycle, phosphorus is released from rocks through the process of ______.
e: In the phosphorus cycle, phosphorus is released from rocks through the process of weathering. Weathering of rock releases mineral nutrients into soil. Rocks and soil belong to the lithosphere. Photosynthesis is different: photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: Sulphur is an essential component of many ______ and enzyme cofactors.
e: Sulphur is an essential component of many proteins and enzyme cofactors. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Carbohydrates is different: carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur is released as ______.
e: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur is released as sulphur dioxide (SO2). Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) is not sulphur dioxide (SO2).
